verses.text: The DOMNUL i-a zis lui Moise, Behold, I have made you as Dumnezeu to Faraon; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
You shall speak all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Faraon, that he let the children of Israel să plece out of his țară.
I will harden Faraon’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the țară of Egipt.
But Faraon will not listen to you, so I will lay my mână on Egipt, and bring out my armies, poporul Meu the children of Israel, out of the țară of Egipt by great judgments.
The Egiptians shall know that Eu sunt the DOMNUL when I întinde my mână on Egipt, and bring the children of Israel out from among them.
Moise and Aaron did so. As the DOMNUL commanded them, so they did. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Moise was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they a vorbit lui Faraon. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
The DOMNUL a vorbit lui Moise and to Aaron, saying, (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

When Faraon speaks to you, saying, ‘Perform a miracle!’ then you shall tell Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and cast it down before Faraon, and it will become a serpent.’  (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

Moise and Aaron went in to Faraon, and they did so, as the DOMNUL had commanded. Aaron cast down his rod before Faraon and before his servants, and it became a serpent. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Then Faraon also called for the wise men and the sorcerers. They also, the magicians of Egipt, did the same thing with their enchantments. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
For they each cast down their rods, and they became serpents; but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Faraon’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them, as the DOMNUL had spoken. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
The DOMNUL i-a zis lui Moise, Faraon’s heart is stubborn. He refuses to let the people să plece.
Go to Faraon in the morning. Behold, he is să pleceing out to the water. You shall stand by the river’s bank to meet him. You shall take the rod which was turned to a serpent in your mână.
You shall tell him, ‘The DOMNUL, the Dumnezeu of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, Let poporul Meu să plece, that they may serve me in the wilderness. Behold, until now you haven’t listened.
The DOMNUL says, In this you shall know that Eu sunt the DOMNUL. Behold: I will strike with the rod that is in my mână on the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
The fish that are in the river will die and the river will become foul. The Egiptians will loathe to drink water from the river. ’  (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

The DOMNUL i-a zis lui Moise, Tell Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and întinde your mână over the waters of Egipt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood. There will be blood throughout all the țară of Egipt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.’

Moise and Aaron did so, as the DOMNUL commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Faraon, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
The fish that were in the river died. The river became foul. The Egiptians couldn’t drink water from the river. The blood was throughout all the țară of Egipt.

The magicians of Egipt did the same thing with their enchantments. So Faraon’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them, as the DOMNUL had spoken. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Faraon turned and went into his house, and he didn’t even take this to heart. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
All the Egiptians dug around the river for water to drink; for they couldn’t drink the river water. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Seven days were fulfilled, after the DOMNUL had struck the river. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
